panels.description: Age of the last completed cycle per node. Yellow at 15m, red at 30m. A flat latency line with a stale cycle means the exporter stalled.
panels.title: Cycle age

panels.description: Age of the last successful config-source fetch per node. The URL source refreshes every 5m (yellow at 15m, red at 30m); the directory source fetches only at startup and SIGHUP.
panels.title: Config fetch age

panels.description: Share of tunnel DNS lookups that answered, averaged over 15m. Address-literal targets have no DNS series.
panels.title: Tunnel DNS up ratio 15m

panels.description: Mean over the selected targets and configs, per node. Raw per-target series remain below. Last successful values only; read with the success ratio above.

panels.description: Mean over the selected targets and configs, per node. Raw per-target series remain below. Last successful values only; read with the success ratio above.
panels.title: DNS lookup: average per node

panels.description: Mean over the selected targets and configs, per node. Raw per-target series remain below. Last successful values only; read with the success ratio above.
panels.title: Total request: average per node

panels.description: Tunnel DNS round trip as a share of TTFB. Rising means name resolution, not transfer, is degrading. Address-literal targets have no DNS series and skew the ratio low.

panels.title: Body transfer: average per node
Network (ipinfo.io)
panels.description: The network each node egresses from, as ipinfo.io reports it. A third party's best guess.

panels.title: Direct controls: share up per node
panels.description: One line per node: the share of its direct probes (ya.ru, google.com, TCP, DNS) that answer, outside any tunnel. A drop means the node's own network is degraded or filtering; pick the node below for the detail.

panels.title: Entry TCP: share of configs reachable per node
panels.description: One line per node: the share of configs whose server address accepts a plain TCP connection from the node, with no xray in between. Low here means the address or port is blocked from that node; high here with a failing tunnel means the protocol is blocked.

panels.title: Direct controls: details for $node
panels.description: Each direct probe of the node picked in the Node variable. Class is domestic or foreign: domestic up with foreign down looks like a whitelist regime, everything down is a dead line.

panels.title: Entry TCP: details for $node
panels.description: A direct TCP connect from the picked node to each config's server address, with no xray in between. It separates a blocked address or port (down) from a blocked protocol (up while the tunnel probe fails).
Targets that answered their last probe, per vantage point and config. up/total is the latest cycle; green at 95% or more, yellow from 80% to 95%, red below 80%.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (instance, config) (xray_probe_up{instance=~"$instance",config=~"$config",target=~"$target"}) / count by (instance, config) (xray_probe_up{instance=~"$instance",config=~"$config",target=~"$target"})

panels.title: Target success

panels.description: Targets whose last probe got no HTTP response, with the last status and attempt time. No rows means every selected target answered.

targets.expr: max by (instance, config, target) (xray_probe_http_status{instance=~"$instance",config=~"$config",target=~"$target"}) and on (instance, config, target) (xray_probe_up{instance=~"$instance",config=~"$config",target=~"$target"} == 0)

max by (instance, config, target) (xray_target_timestamp_seconds{instance=~"$instance",config=~"$config",target=~"$target"}) * 1000 and on (instance, config, target) (xray_probe_up{instance=~"$instance",config=~"$config",target=~"$target"} == 0)

panels.title: Failing targets

panels.description: One row per instance, config and target whose probe failed at least once in the selected time range. Red means the last probe got no HTTP response, green means the target answered. Only probes that failed get a row, so the panel stays focused on outages; an empty panel means nothing failed in this range.

targets.expr: max by (instance, config, target) (xray_probe_up{instance=~"$instance",config=~"$config",target=~"$target"}) and on (instance, config, target) (min_over_time(xray_probe_up{instance=~"$instance",config=~"$config",target=~"$target"}[$__range] @ end()) == 0)

panels.title: Failing targets timeline

panels.description: HTTP status of the last probe. 0 means no response; 2xx green, 3xx blue, 4xx orange, 5xx red.
